Who took you in, after the vats?
Nobody raised you: you were made. Who did you fall in with once you were let out?
A farm that bought you as a field hand
A farmer bought you off the Tinkerer's cart to pull a plough, and you learned to work before you learned to talk.
A field hand, bought off a cart.
A mine that put you to work
A mine bought you to haul ore where nobody else would go, and you grew strong carrying it.
Hauling ore in a mine.
A ship that signed you on, no questions asked
A captain who asked no questions put you on the oars, and you learned to keep your feet on a rolling deck.
At the oars, no questions asked.
Trappers who caught you running wild
Trappers caught you running wild in the woods, and kept you because you tracked as well as their dogs.
Caught wild, kept by trappers.
A sideshow merchant who showed you off
A sideshow merchant showed you off from town to town, and you learned to count coin and read the faces that stared.
A sideshow merchant's exhibit.
A warlord who meant you for the front line
A warlord bought you for the front line and drilled you like a hound, and you outlived every plan they had for you.
Bought for a warlord's front line.
Temple healers who kept your seams closed
Temple healers took you in when your seams kept splitting, and you learned what a body, even yours, needs to mend.
Healers who kept your seams closed.
A hedge-wizard who wanted to study you
A hedge-wizard bought you to study, and you ended up grinding his powders and reading his notes on yourself.
A hedge-wizard's study, then his helper.
Outlaws who broke you out of a cage
Outlaws broke open the cage you were being carted in, and from them you learned to move quietly and leave no trace.
Broken out of a cage by outlaws.
Nobody: you raised yourself
Nobody wanted you. You were let out of the vats into the world and worked out the rest on your own.
Nobody. You raised yourself.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.childho: In your first months, you were always...
The vat-born grow up fast. What filled those first months?
Leaping in the moonlight to test your new legs
In your first months you were always out in the moonlight, testing how far your new legs would leap and landing lighter than anything stitched together should.
Testing new legs in the moonlight.
Hiding in caves from the folk who stared
In your first months you were always hiding in caves from the folk who stared, and the dark felt more like home than any house.
Hiding in caves from staring folk.
Fighting anything that called you a monster
In your first months you fought anything that called you a monster, and when you lost you got up and went again.
Fighting all who called you monster.
Reading everything to learn what you were
In your first months you read anything you could find to learn what you were, and kept asking how much time you had.
Reading to learn what you were.
Sinking to the bottom to see how long you'd last
In your first months you sank to the bottom of every pond to see how long you could last, and the deep never frightened you.
Sinking to see how long you'd last.
Standing out in the storms, though lightning hurt you most
In your first months you stood out in every storm while everyone else ran indoors, though the lightning hurt you worst of all.
Standing out in the storms.
Sitting too close to the fire, just to feel warm
In your first months you sat too close to every fire just to feel warm, and somehow the smoke never bothered you.
Too close to the fire, to feel warm.
Lying out in the snow to see what the cold would do
In your first months you lay out in the snow to see what the cold would do to you, long after you stopped feeling your fingers.
Lying in the snow, testing the cold.
Listening to the bells from outside the walls
In your first months you lay outside the town walls listening to the bells at night, and swore you could hear more than one note.
Bells heard from outside the walls.
Collecting every scrap you came across
In your first months you collected every scrap you came across, a blade, a buckle, a spare part like yours, and knew every piece of it by heart.
Collecting every blade and scrap.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.youth.s: You were made full grown in a season. What did you do with it?
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.youth.c: Once you were full grown you ran with the Ash Whisperer's cutpurses, who found that a face like yours made folk look away from their purses.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.youth.l: Marched at the very front of a war camp's line
Once you were full grown a realm's war camp put you at the very front of its line, and you learned to lead it.
Leading the line from the front.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.youth.a: Swept floors for a court wizard who studied you
Once you were full grown you swept a court wizard's floors, and read his books while he took notes on you.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.youth.h: Once you were full grown the elements answered when you called, and an old elemental school took you in, mostly to keep an eye on you.
Once you were full grown you hunted with the Green Huntsman's folk, and found that most of what you hunted was weaker than you.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.youth.w: Once you were full grown you lived off the land through hard winters that killed better-made things than you. Nobody taught you. The wild did.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.youth.p: Fought in the pits, billed as the monster
Once you were full grown you fought in the pits for coin, billed as the monster, and learned to take a hit.
Billed as the monster in the pits.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.youth.g: Once you were full grown a ship's master gunner took you on, since nobody minded if a gun blew up in your face.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.youth.m: Carried messages on the one horse that would bear you
Once you were full grown you found the one horse in a realm's stables that would let you near it, and carried messages on it from one end of the land to the other.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.biobuilt.turn.su: Something happened that even your maker never planned for.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.rubberfolk.raise: Who raised you on the road?
The fair never stayed anywhere long. Who looked after you in it?
Farmers who took you in when the fair moved on
The fair left you behind at a farm one autumn, and the farmers who took you in had you working beside them from first light.
Left at a farm when the fair moved on.
Your family ran the fair's stalls, and you learned to count coin and read a face before you could walk straight.
The fair's fortune-teller took you in and set you to grinding her powders and copying out fortunes that never came true.
Your family worked the crowds while the acts played, and you learned to move quietly and leave no trace.
Nobody: the fair moved on without you
Nobody claimed you. The fair packed up one night and left you asleep in the field, and you were raised by whoever was kind that year.
Nobody. Left behind by the fair.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.rubberfolk.child: Bouncing off the wagon roofs in the moonlight
As a child you were always bouncing off the wagon roofs in the moonlight, leaping further than you should have and landing lighter than you had any right to.
As a child you collected everything you came across, the knife-thrower's knives, a buckle, a broken bow, and knew every piece of it by heart.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.rubberfolk.youth: Wrestled all comers in the fair's ring
As you grew up you wrestled all comers in the fair's ring for coin, and learned to take a hit and bounce back.
Wrestling all comers in the ring.
Who found you, and raised you?
Nobody knows where you came from. Who took you in?
Fisherfolk who pulled you from the oasis
Fisherfolk pulled you out of the temple's oasis and raised you as their own, and you learned to keep your feet on a rolling deck.
Pulled from the oasis by fisherfolk.
Farmers took you in from the oasis and you worked the land beside them, though you were always happiest in the ditches when the water ran.
Nobody claimed you. You grew up alone in the shallows by the old temple, and the sea fed you.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.stoneborn.raised: Your family's place in the hold shaped your first years.
Mushroom farmers in the deep halls
Your parents farmed mushrooms in the deep halls by lamplight, and you worked beside them.
Mushroom farmers in the deep halls.
Miners and smiths of the hold
Your family cut ore from the mountain's heart and beat it into tools, and you grew strong carrying it.
Fishers of the black lakes under the mountain
Your family fished the black lakes under the mountain, and you learned to keep your feet on a raft in the dark.
Hunters who tracked in the dark by sound
Your family hunted the deep tunnels by sound alone, and you learned to keep a steady hand in the dark.
Traders who carried the hold's iron to the towns
Your family carried the hold's iron down to the towns, and you learned to count coin and read a face.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.stoneborn.childh: Climbing the hold's great pillars by lamplight
As a child you were always climbing the hold's great pillars, leaping further than you should have and landing lighter than you had any right to.
Swimming the black lakes under the mountain
As a child you always swam further out into the black lakes than anyone dared, and the deep never frightened you.
Climbing out onto the peaks to watch the storms
As a child you were always climbing out of the hold to watch the storm clouds roll in, while everyone else stayed safe below.
Up on the peaks, watching storms.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.sylvan.raised.su: The old forest raises its own. Who had the most hand in you?
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.sylvan.raised.fa: Your parents tended the forest's wild orchards from first light, and you worked beside them in the branches.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.sylvan.raised.hu: Your family hunted from the high branches, and you learned to keep a steady hand on a swaying bough.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.sylvan.childhood: Leaping between the branches in the moonlight
As a child you were always out leaping between the branches in the moonlight, further than you should have and landing lighter than you had any right to.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.verdant.raised.s: In a Verdant village everyone raises the children. Who had the most hand in you?
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.verdant.raised.f: Moss farmers under the green sky
Your parents tended the moss fields under the green sky, and you worked beside them in the sun.
Moss farmers under the green sky.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.verdant.raised.s: Your parents fought for the Verdant villages, and trained you as soon as you could stand.
Verdant warriors who trained you young.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.verdant.raised.m: Traders who crossed between the worlds
Your family carried goods through the gate between the worlds, and you learned to count coin and read a stranger's face.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.emberborn.raised: The expedition never went home. Who raised you at the Nether's edge?
Your family dug the Nether's ore and worked it at forges that never cooled, and you grew strong carrying it.
Your parents guarded the expedition's walls against whatever came out of the portal, and drilled you as soon as you could hold a stick.
Your family tended the expedition's burned and broken, and you learned what the body needs to mend.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.emberborn.childh: Daring yourself into the snow, though it sapped you
As a child you dared yourself out into the snow though the cold sapped you, and stayed long after your fingers went numb.
Daring the snow, though it sapped you.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.frostborn.raised: Your people settled the snowfields, and everyone who lives through the winter helps raise the children. Who raised you?
Your parents drove their herds across the snowfields from first light, and you walked beside them.
Your family fished through holes in the lake ice, and you learned to keep your feet on ice that groaned.
Your family lived off what they could track through the long winter, and you learned to keep a steady hand in the cold.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.frostborn.childh: Swimming under the ice further than anyone dared
As a child you always swam further under the ice than anyone dared, and the deep never frightened you.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.nightborn.raised: Your mother's people kept to the night. Who raised you among them?
Your parents worked the moor's fields by lantern light, and you worked beside them till dawn.
Your family hunted the moors after dark, and you learned to keep a steady hand by starlight.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.warriorborn.rais: Who raised you in the camp?
The warband raised its children together. Who had the most hand in you?
Camp-followers who fed the warband
Your parents foraged and cooked for the warband from first light, and you hauled beside them.
Camp-followers who fed the band.
The warband's armourers
Your family kept the warband's blades and armour mended on the march, and you grew strong carrying the anvil.
The warband's armourers.
Sutlers who trailed the warband
Your family trailed the warband selling to its fighters, and you learned to count coin and read a face.
Sutlers trailing the warband.
The warband's fighters
Your parents fought in the warband's front rank, and drilled you as soon as you could hold a stick.
The warband's fighters.
The warband's bone-setters
Your family set the warband's bones after every fight, and you learned what the body needs to mend.
The warband's bone-setters.
Nobody: the band's pods left without you
Nobody claimed you. The band went back up in its pods one night and you were not in one, and you were raised by whoever was kind that year, which was not many once they saw the tail.
Nobody. The pods left without you.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.warriorborn.chil: As a child you trained like your life depended on it, because in the camp it did: running, lifting, striking, until your hands bled and you went again.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.earthling.raised: In the city of towers, everyone had a trade. What was your family's?
A scholar took you in and set you to grinding his powders and copying his notes in a tower full of arguments.
On the high desert, every family lives by the wells. What was yours?
Your parents worked the oasis gardens before the heat came up, and you worked beside them.
Your family kept the wells and poled boats down the desert river, and you learned to keep your feet on a rocking hull.
Your family drove caravans across the sands between the oases, and you learned to count coin and read a face.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.dawnborn.childho: Climbing the far peaks to touch the snow
As a child you were always climbing the far peaks to build forts in the only snow you'd ever seen, long after your fingers went numb.
Chasing the only snow you'd seen.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.beastfolk.raised: Who raised you in the wild?
Beastfolk dens raise their young together. Who had the most hand in you?
Foragers who knew every root and berry
Your parents foraged the wild lands from first light, and you followed them by scent to every root and berry patch.
Foragers of the wild lands.
Den-diggers who worked bone and flint
Your family dug the dens and knapped flint and bone into tools, and you grew strong hauling stone out of the earth.
Den-diggers who worked bone and flint.
Fishers of the wild rivers
Your family fished the wild rivers with spear and paw, and you learned to keep your feet on slick stones in the current.
Fishers of the wild rivers.
The den's hunters
Your family ran down game for the whole den, and you learned to stalk downwind and strike before you were heard.
The den's hunters.
Fur-traders who dealt with the towns
Your family carried furs and herbs to the town markets, and you learned to count coin and read a face that didn't trust yours.
Fur-traders to the towns.
The den's guard
Your parents stood guard over the den against wolves, raiders and worse, and drilled you as soon as you could hold a stick.
The den's guard.
The den's herb-healers
Your family tended the den's hurt with chewed herbs and moss, and you learned what the body needs to mend.
The den's herb-healers.
A wise one who read the bones
The den's wise one took you in, and set you to grinding herbs and learning what the thrown bones say.
A bone-reader's helper.
Raiders who robbed the roads
Your family robbed the roads where the towns' carts ran close to the wild, and you learned to move quietly and leave no scent.
Road-raiders who left no scent.
A realm's beast-kin household
Your family held a small title in %s, a rare thing for beastfolk, and you learned the manners of a court that never stopped staring.
A rare beast-kin title in %s.
Nobody: you were left in the wild
Nobody claimed you. You were left at the edge of the wild and raised yourself on what you could catch.
Nobody. You raised yourself in the wild.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.beastfolk.childh: As a cub, you were always...
Every cub in the den runs wild. What kind of cub were you?
Leaping through the treetops in the moonlight
As a cub you were always out leaping through the treetops in the moonlight, further than you should have and landing lighter than you had any right to.
Exploring every burrow and cave near the den
As a cub you were always nosing into every burrow and cave near the den, coming home scraped and filthy and grinning.
As a cub you play-fought every other cub in the den until it stopped being play: tooth and claw, until you bled and went again.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.frostborn.raised: Miners and wrights of the peaks
Your family dug the peaks' ore and worked it the way their grandparents were taught somewhere colder, and you grew strong carrying it.
Miners and wrights of the peaks.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.nightborn.raised: Healers who kept the Lantern Warden's hours
Your family tended the sick through the night by the Lantern Warden's light, and you learned what the body needs to mend.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.stoneborn.raised: Your family set the bones the mountain broke, and you learned what the body needs to mend.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.frostborn.raised: Nobody here: you came from Hail alone
Nobody raised you here. You are a traveller, come down from Hail alone on one of your people's ships, with their glass on your brow and no one on this world who knows your name.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.frostborn.from_f: You were born on Hail, far past the sun, where the cold never lifts and none of your people would have it any other way.
story.jaymoskingdoms.as.emberborn.raised: Nobody claimed you. The expedition lost you somewhere at the Nether's edge, and you were raised by the heat and by whoever was kind that year.
